title: Ballsh oil workers’ public march and road blockade over unpaid wages and government action
location: Ballsh, near the town hall and main road
scope: A public protest action within a continuing Ballsh refinery wage-arrears campaign; campaign onset predates this unit and qualifying-event ownership is unresolved.
organizer: Ballsh refinery workers; specific organizer not established
participants_original: Hundreds of refinery workers and local residents participated in the 12 October public march and road blockade, according to Citizens.al. This is a qualitative count.
threshold_50_evidence: Citizens.al’s 13 October account says Monday’s action brought hundreds of refinery workers and local residents; this establishes at least 50 for the 12 October public action. It does not establish whether an earlier action in the campaign first crossed 50 before October.

start_date.summary: The 13 October reports describe the prior day’s march and road blockade.

location.summary: Reports place the action in Ballsh by the town hall/main road and at the refinery.

state_target.summary: Workers sought unpaid wages and called on Albanian authorities, the Prime Minister, and area representatives to intervene with the refinery company.

demands.summary: The reporting identifies wage arrears and demands for state action to resolve the dispute.

participants_original.summary: Citizens.al says hundreds of workers and local residents took part in the Monday public action.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The qualitative term hundreds establishes more than 50 for the 12 October action.

protester_violence.summary: No evidence of protester violence is recorded; unknown.

state_response.summary: October reports describe no government communication initially and a later invitation to dialogue; no meeting or concession is established. Private security at the refinery is not coded as state response.

notes: The 12 October public march/road blockade has the first clear 50+ evidence located in this research. Related refinery protest activity is reported on 14 September (S013) and 17 September (S011), before this unit; the earliest qualifying crowd size in that campaign remains unknown. Ten workers beginning a hunger strike on 28 September (S006) is not itself evidence of a 50-person gathering. Do not treat missing earlier headcounts as zero. Top Channel search result S014 suggests another large action but its encoded URL returned HTTP 403; no body was read and its date/event identity are unverified.
open_questions: Did a Ballsh public protest of 50 or more occur before October, and which month owns the episode?
What was the response at the protest site on 12 October?
When did the wage-arrears campaign end, and was the November meeting followed by a resolution?

title: Tirana protest against compulsory outdoor mask wearing
location: Outside the Prime Minister’s office, Tirana
organizer: Not established; Exit reports Facebook-organized mobilization
participants_original: CNA reports approximately 50 people; Exit describes tens. The two descriptions leave the exact threshold uncertain.
threshold_50_evidence: CNA’s contemporaneous report gives an approximate count of 50, while Exit’s account uses a qualitative term translating as tens. The approximate estimate does not provide a secure numeric lower bound of 50; pending confirmation.

start_date.summary: CNA dates the gathering to 15 October; Exit’s next-day article places it the prior evening.

location.summary: Reports place participants outside the Prime Minister’s office in Tirana.

state_target.summary: Participants opposed the government’s mandatory mask rule for outdoor/public spaces.

demands.summary: The demand was withdrawal/rejection of compulsory outdoor mask wearing.

participants_original.summary: CNA reports approximately 50; Exit says tens. These are not equivalent threshold evidence.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Approx. 50 could be near but not safely above the cutoff; Exit’s qualitative tens does not independently establish 50.

protester_violence.summary: CNA mentions a clash without specifying its conduct; burning masks is not coded as violence against the state.

state_response.summary: Exit says police dispersed the gathering and some were taken into custody; CNA reports three people escorted to a police station. No separate evidence of beatings or firearms.

notes: CNA’s count is approximate, so the 50-person criterion remains pending despite the point estimate. Reports describe police dispersal and custody/escort to a station. Formal arrest status is not independently established by CNA’s wording. No Facebook page or post was opened; the organizer attribution is secondary-source reporting.
open_questions: Does any independent contemporaneous source establish a count clearly at or above 50?
Were the three people formally arrested, or only escorted/processed?

title: Tirana demonstration over Albania’s position toward Greece and the Cham issue
location: Outside Albania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Tirana
organizer: PDIU, Çamëria and other political groups, according to Euronews Albania
participants_original: No total crowd estimate was reported. Police initiated criminal proceedings against 18 people; that number describes those processed, not the total crowd.
threshold_50_evidence: Neither the State Police release nor Euronews Albania reports total attendance. Eighteen people being processed does not establish that 50 or more attended.

start_date.summary: Both reports concern the 20 October gathering before the Foreign Ministry.

location.summary: The gathering took place outside Albania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tirana.

state_target.summary: The report says the protest addressed Albania’s government position toward Greece, including the Cham issue and maritime delimitation; this is an own-state policy demand.

demands.summary: Political demand concerning Albania’s government position toward Greece and the Cham issue.

participants_original.summary: No crowd count; 18 refers to people facing criminal proceedings.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Attendance is unquantified; prosecutions cannot be used as a crowd count.

protester_violence.summary: No evidence of protester violence is recorded; unknown.

state_response.summary: Police warned the crowd, dispersed the gathering, issued mask fines and opened criminal proceedings against 18 people. Proceedings do not by themselves establish arrests.

notes: The stated demand concerns Albania’s own government position, not solely Greece’s policy. The political-group organizers and foreign-policy issue require review against the codebook’s exclusion for election-associated political rallies; reporting does not describe an upcoming-election rally. Criminal proceedings against 18 do not equal arrests.
open_questions: Does the gathering meet the project’s distinction between a government-targeted protest and a political rally?

title: Possible Tirana health-worker gathering over dismissal of a whistleblowing doctor
scope: Possible single-day local gathering; details are limited
participants_original: CIVICUS says health workers gathered but gives no count.
threshold_50_evidence: No participant total or clear crowd-size description was reported.

start_date.summary: CIVICUS’s February 2021 review dates the gathering to 31 October 2020.

location.summary: CIVICUS places health workers outside Mother Teresa hospital in Tirana.

state_target.summary: The gathering opposed a doctor’s dismissal from the public hospital, but the report does not specify a demand addressed to the government or identify the decision-maker.

demands.summary: The report ties the gathering to dismissal of a doctor who had spoken to media; the requested remedy is not specified.

participants_original.summary: CIVICUS reports health workers gathered, with no number.

notes: CIVICUS’s title and most of the page concern December 2020, but the relevant paragraph separately reports a 31 October health-worker gathering. Its page date is 23 February 2021. The report cites TV Klan for this item, but that linked article was not retrieved; size and explicit state-directed demand remain unknown. No threshold or government-target conclusion is inferred from plural 'health workers' alone.
open_questions: What demand/remedy did participants press, and was the state the target?
What does the cited TV Klan report say about the gathering?
